option_description: Whether the CA builds the certificate Subject/SAN from a trusted directory/identity source so a low-privileged requester cannot dictate identity (true = secure: CT_FLAG_SUBJECT_REQUIRE_DIRECTORY_PATH set / EJBCA 'Allow Subject DN Override by CSR' disabled).
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "Weak issuance authorization (enrollee-supplied identity)" — fires when false (CT_FLAG_ENROLLEE_SUPPLIES_SUBJECT set on a template carrying an auth EKU with low-priv enrollment and no approval), the ESC1 root cause that lets any enrollee mint a cert with a domain admin's UPN in the SAN.

how_to_obtain.instruction: AD CS: enumerate templates and the mspki-certificate-name-flag, cross-checking with Certify.exe or PSPKIAudit for vulnerable subject handling.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Secure: CT_FLAG_SUBJECT_REQUIRE_DIRECTORY_PATH (subject built from directory). Insecure: CT_FLAG_ENROLLEE_SUPPLIES_SUBJECT set on a template with an auth EKU + low-priv enroll + no manager approval (ESC1).
how_to_obtain.source: SpecterOps — Certified Pre-Owned: Abusing Active Directory Certificate Services (ESC1-ESC8)

how_to_obtain.instruction: EJBCA: inspect the Certificate Profile field 'Allow Subject DN Override by CSR' and 'Allow Extension Override' in the admin GUI / profile export.
how_to_obtain.navigation: EJBCA Admin GUI -> Certificate Profiles -> <profile> -> Allow Subject DN Override by CSR / Allow Extension Override
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Secure: 'Allow Subject DN Override by CSR' = disabled, 'Allow Extension Override' = disabled (or restrictive allowlist). Insecure: enabled, letting the CSR dictate identity.
how_to_obtain.source: EJBCA (Keyfactor) — Certificate Profile Fields

option_description: Whether an enrollee-reachable template grants an authentication-capable EKU (Client Authentication 1.3.6.1.5.5.7.3.2, PKINIT Client Auth 1.3.6.1.5.2.3.4, or Smart Card Logon 1.3.6.1.4.1.311.20.2.2) that turns a requested SAN into domain authentication.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "Weak issuance authorization (enrollee-supplied identity)" — combined with requester-supplied subject and no approval, an auth EKU on a low-priv-enrollable template is what makes an ESC1 SAN abusable as domain logon.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review pKIExtendedKeyUsage per template; flag templates granting auth EKUs enrollable by broad groups.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Insecure: Any Purpose / empty EKU / auth EKU on a template enrollable by broad groups. Secure: scoped EKU OIDs matching the certificate's real purpose.
how_to_obtain.source: SpecterOps — Certified Pre-Owned: Abusing Active Directory Certificate Services (ESC1-ESC8)

how_to_obtain.instruction: EJBCA: review the Certificate Profile Extended Key Usage field — confirm scoped OIDs, not blanket assignment.
how_to_obtain.navigation: EJBCA Admin GUI -> Certificate Profiles -> <profile> -> Extended Key Usage
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Secure: explicit EKU OIDs per RFC 5280 for the intended use; avoid broad assignments.
how_to_obtain.source: EJBCA (Keyfactor) — Certificate Profile Fields

option_description: Whether issuance for any template allowing requester-supplied subject/SAN (or carrying an auth/SubCA/enrollment-agent EKU) is held pending Certificate Manager approval or a required RA signature (CT_FLAG_PEND_ALL_REQUESTS / msPKI-RA-Signature).
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "Weak issuance authorization (enrollee-supplied identity)" — fires when false (auto-issue with no manager approval), removing the compensating control that neutralises ESC1.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Check msPKI-Enrollment-Flag for CT_FLAG_PEND_ALL_REQUESTS and msPKI-RA-Signature for required authorized signatures on sensitive templates.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Secure: PEND_ALL_REQUESTS set (or RA signatures required) on sensitive templates. Insecure: neither — request auto-issues.
how_to_obtain.source: Microsoft Learn — Securing PKI: Technical Controls for Securing PKI

option_description: Whether a low-privilege-enrollable template grants the Any Purpose EKU (2.5.29.37.0) or carries no EKU at all (subordinate-CA capable), yielding a certificate usable for any purpose including authentication or sub-CA creation (ESC2).
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "Weak issuance authorization (enrollee-supplied identity)" — fires when true (Any Purpose or empty EKU enrollable), the ESC2 primitive.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review pKIExtendedKeyUsage per template; flag templates with Any Purpose (2.5.29.37.0), no EKU, or auth EKUs enrollable by Domain Users.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Insecure: Any Purpose / empty EKU / auth EKU on a template enrollable by broad groups. Secure: scoped EKU OIDs matching the certificate's real purpose.
how_to_obtain.source: SpecterOps — Certified Pre-Owned: Abusing Active Directory Certificate Services (ESC1-ESC8)

how_to_obtain.instruction: EJBCA: confirm the Certificate Profile Extended Key Usage uses scoped OIDs and no blanket/Any Purpose assignment.
how_to_obtain.navigation: EJBCA Admin GUI -> Certificate Profiles -> <profile> -> Extended Key Usage
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Secure: explicit EKU OIDs per RFC 5280 for the intended use; avoid broad assignments.
how_to_obtain.source: EJBCA (Keyfactor) — Certificate Profile Fields

option_description: Whether the CA-wide 'allow user-defined SAN in request attribute' policy flag is disabled (AD CS: EDITF_ATTRIBUTESUBJECTALTNAME2 absent from policy\EditFlags). True = secure.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "CA-wide SAN injection / issuance-control bypass" — fires when false (EDITF_ATTRIBUTESUBJECTALTNAME2 present), the ESC6 flag that globally re-enables ESC1-style impersonation across every template regardless of per-template hardening.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read the CA policy EditFlags and confirm the SAN-attribute flag is absent.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Secure: EDITF_ATTRIBUTESUBJECTALTNAME2 NOT listed. Insecure: it appears in the EditFlags value. Disable with: certutil -setreg policy\EditFlags -EDITF_ATTRIBUTESUBJECTALTNAME2 then net stop certsvc && net start certsvc.
how_to_obtain.source: Microsoft Learn — Securing PKI: Technical Controls for Securing PKI

option_description: Whether CA-management rights (ManageCA / 'CA administrator' role) are restricted to dedicated Tier-0 admin accounts and withheld from broad/unprivileged principals, so the CA-wide SAN policy flag cannot be silently re-flipped.
security_impact: An OR-trigger for both "CA-wide SAN injection / issuance-control bypass" and "Weak / default CA admin access and role separation" — fires when false (ESC7), where a broad/low-priv ManageCA holder can flip EDITF_ATTRIBUTESUBJECTALTNAME2 at will, voiding every per-template control.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review the CA security descriptor / ACEs for the ManageCA right; PSPKIAudit Get-AuditCASecurity flags unprivileged principals.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Secure: only dedicated CA admins/officers hold ManageCA. Insecure: low-priv or broad groups granted this (ESC7).
how_to_obtain.source: SpecterOps — Certified Pre-Owned: Abusing Active Directory Certificate Services (ESC1-ESC8)

option_description: Whether the issuing/subordinate CA certificate carries an X.509 NameConstraints extension (permitted/excluded DNS, IP, email, directory subtrees) scoping which identities it may ever sign, bound to the org's owned namespaces.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "Unconstrained / over-trusted issuing CA" — fires when false (no NameConstraints), letting the CA (or a stolen subordinate key) mint certificates for ANY name including domains it does not own.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Dump the issuing CA cert and inspect the Name Constraints extension.
how_to_obtain.command: openssl x509 -in issuing-ca.crt -noout -text | grep -A10 'X509v3 Name Constraints'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Secure: 'Permitted'/'Excluded' subtrees scoping DNS/email/dirName to owned namespaces. Insecure: extension absent — CA can issue for any name.
how_to_obtain.source: general-knowledge

how_to_obtain.instruction: EJBCA: confirm Name Constraints (permitted/excluded) are configured on CA-type Certificate Profiles.
how_to_obtain.navigation: EJBCA Admin GUI -> Certificate Profiles -> <CA profile> -> Name Constraints
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Secure: permitted/excluded name subtrees defined. Note: EJBCA does not validate path length at issuance, so constraints must be set deliberately.
how_to_obtain.source: EJBCA (Keyfactor) — Certificate Profile Fields

option_description: Whether the issuing CA certificate's BasicConstraints pathLenConstraint is set to bound how many further intermediate CAs may chain below it (pathLen=0 on a leaf issuing CA = no further sub-CAs).
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "Unconstrained / over-trusted issuing CA" — fires when false (pathLen unset/over-large), letting the CA spawn rogue subordinate CAs. EJBCA does not validate path length at issuance, so it must be set deliberately.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Dump the issuing CA cert and inspect Basic Constraints for the pathlen value.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Secure: 'CA:TRUE, pathlen:0' on the issuing CA. Insecure: CA:TRUE with no pathlen, permitting rogue sub-CA creation.
how_to_obtain.source: EJBCA (Keyfactor) — Certificate Profile Fields

option_description: Whether the trust-anchor root (and policy CA) is kept offline and separated from online issuing/subordinate CAs, rather than a flat hierarchy with an online root signing leaf certs or a CA co-located with a domain controller.
security_impact: A secondary OR-trigger for "Unconstrained / over-trusted issuing CA" — fires when false (online root issuing leaves or Tier-0 co-location), amplifying the blast radius so a single compromise forges unlimited trust across namespaces.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review the PKI hierarchy: confirm a distinct offline root, separate online issuing CA(s), and that no CA is co-located with a DC. For cloud CAs, confirm root in its own account with minimized root use.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Secure: offline root, constrained subordinates, isolated roles. Insecure: online root issuing leaves, or CA sharing a host with other Tier-0 roles.
how_to_obtain.source: AWS Private CA — Best practices

option_description: The custody tier of the CA signing key: HSM/KMS-backed (hsm_fips_l3, hsm_fips_l2) where disk-image theft is worthless, vs software_non_exportable (still recoverable from a disk image) and software_exportable (any local admin exports the on-disk PEM / DPAPI key).
security_impact: The primary OR-trigger for "CA signing-key theft (no HSM custody)" — fires when in [software_exportable, software_non_exportable], letting a local admin export the key and forge unlimited trusted certificates off-box.

how_to_obtain.instruction: AD CS: confirm the CSP/KSP provider — a hardware KSP vs 'Microsoft Software Key Storage Provider' (which indicates NO HSM); generic: check whether the signing key sits on disk vs a KMS/HSM URI.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Secure: provider names a hardware KSP/HSM (e.g. nCipher, Luna); key non-exportable. Insecure: 'Microsoft Software Key Storage Provider' / a readable ca-key.pem on disk.
how_to_obtain.source: Microsoft Learn — Securing PKI: Protecting CA Keys and Critical Artifacts

how_to_obtain.instruction: cfssl/step/smallstep/sigstore: confirm the signing key is referenced via a KMS/HSM URI rather than a local key file path.
how_to_obtain.file_path: CA config (e.g. ca.json / cfssl config / ca.cfg)
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Secure: KMS/PKCS#11 URI (awskms://, gcpkms://, azurekms://, hashivault://, pkcs11:) for the signing key. Insecure: a plaintext on-disk key file path.
how_to_obtain.source: Sigstore Cosign — KMS key management overview

option_description: Whether routine backups bundle an exportable CA signing-key PFX onto general backup infrastructure (full system-state / certutil -backup) rather than DB-only backups with the key PFX isolated under chain-of-custody.
security_impact: An OR-trigger for "CA signing-key theft (no HSM custody)" — fires when true, where the key is reachable from shared backup systems and a brute-forceable PFX hands an attacker the whole PKI.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review the backup job: confirm it uses 'certutil -backupdb' or 'Backup-CARoleService -DatabaseOnly' (key excluded), and that any key PFX is stored offline with monitored access — not on shared backup systems.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Secure: DB-only routine backups; key PFX isolated. Insecure: full -backup/system-state including the key reachable from the backup server.
how_to_obtain.source: Microsoft Learn — Securing PKI: Technical Controls for Securing PKI

option_description: Whether an HTTP-based enrollment endpoint (AD CS Web Enrollment /certsrv, CES/CEP, or NDES /CertSrv/mscep) is reachable on this CA. The relay attack surface exists only when such an endpoint is present.
security_impact: An OR-trigger (the gating precondition) for "NTLM relay to HTTP enrollment endpoint" — fires when true; if web enrollment is removed entirely the ESC8 vector is closed.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Probe for the web-enrollment endpoints (http(s)://<ca>/certsrv, /CertSrv/mscep for NDES) and confirm whether they are present and reachable on the CA host.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Secure: endpoints removed/absent (connection refused / 404). Insecure: /certsrv, CES/CEP, or NDES /CertSrv/mscep present and reachable (ESC8 relay surface exists).
how_to_obtain.source: SpecterOps — Certified Pre-Owned: Abusing Active Directory Certificate Services (ESC1-ESC8)

option_description: Whether the web-enrollment / CES-CEP / NDES endpoints are served HTTPS-only (plain HTTP bindings removed). True = secure.
security_impact: An OR-trigger for "NTLM relay to HTTP enrollment endpoint" — fires when false (HTTP accepted), letting coerced NTLM auth be relayed over an unprotected channel to obtain an auth-capable certificate (ESC8).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Verify the IIS/enrollment site bindings expose HTTPS only and that plain-HTTP bindings are removed on /certsrv, CES/CEP, and NDES.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Secure: plain HTTP refused / redirects to HTTPS only; only HTTPS bindings present. Insecure: HTTP binding answers on the enrollment endpoint.
how_to_obtain.source: SpecterOps — Certified Pre-Owned: Abusing Active Directory Certificate Services (ESC1-ESC8)

option_description: Whether IIS Extended Protection for Authentication (EPA / channel binding) is set to Required on the Windows Authentication of the enrollment endpoints, binding the authentication to the TLS channel.
security_impact: An OR-trigger for "NTLM relay to HTTP enrollment endpoint" — fires when false; EPA Required defeats cross-protocol NTLM relay to the enrollment endpoint (ESC8).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Check the enrollment site's Windows Authentication Advanced Settings for Extended Protection = Required.
how_to_obtain.navigation: IIS Manager -> <enrollment site> -> Authentication -> Windows Authentication -> Advanced Settings -> Extended Protection
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Secure: Extended Protection = Required (channel binding enforced). Insecure: Off / Accept — relay possible.
how_to_obtain.source: SpecterOps — Certified Pre-Owned: Abusing Active Directory Certificate Services (ESC1-ESC8)

option_description: Whether NTLM is disabled on the HTTP enrollment endpoints (Kerberos/Negotiate-only), so coerced NTLM auth cannot be relayed there at all.
security_impact: An OR-trigger for "NTLM relay to HTTP enrollment endpoint" — fires when false; disabling NTLM removes the relayed credential the ESC8 chain depends on.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Verify the enrollment endpoints accept Kerberos/Negotiate only and that NTLM is disabled (site auth providers / network policy).
how_to_obtain.navigation: IIS Manager -> <enrollment site> -> Authentication -> Windows Authentication -> Providers (Negotiate only, NTLM removed)
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Secure: only Kerberos/Negotiate offered; NTLM removed from providers / blocked by policy. Insecure: NTLM accepted on the enrollment endpoint.
how_to_obtain.source: SpecterOps — Certified Pre-Owned: Abusing Active Directory Certificate Services (ESC1-ESC8)

option_description: Whether the ManageCertificates (Certificate Manager) issuance/approval permission is restricted to dedicated, vetted certificate-officer accounts and not held by broad or unprivileged principals.
security_impact: An OR-trigger for "Weak / default CA admin access and role separation" — fires when false (granted broadly), where a holder can approve their own pending request, bypassing manager approval (ESC7).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review the CA security descriptor / ACEs for the ManageCertificates right; PSPKIAudit Get-AuditCASecurity flags unprivileged principals.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Secure: only dedicated CA admins/officers hold ManageCertificates. Insecure: low-priv or broad groups granted this (ESC7).
how_to_obtain.source: SpecterOps — Certified Pre-Owned: Abusing Active Directory Certificate Services (ESC1-ESC8)

option_description: Whether MFA / smart-card is enforced for interactive CA management access and CA admins use dedicated alternate (not daily-driver) accounts.
security_impact: An OR-trigger for "Weak / default CA admin access and role separation" — fires when false (password-only console access), easing credential abuse on ManageCA/ManageCertificates holders.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm MFA / smart-card enforced for interactive CA access and that CA admins use dedicated alternate accounts, not daily-driver accounts.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Secure: MFA + dedicated admin accounts. Insecure: shared/daily accounts, password-only console access.
how_to_obtain.source: Microsoft Learn — Securing PKI: Technical Controls for Securing PKI

option_description: Whether Common-Criteria role separation is enforced so no single identity holds both ManageCA and ManageCertificates (admin vs issuer vs auditor vs backup duties split), and the setting is change-monitored.
security_impact: An OR-trigger for "Weak / default CA admin access and role separation" — fires when false (role separation off/unset), where one account both weakens policy and approves issuance.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read the CA RoleSeparationEnabled registry value (1 = enabled), and confirm the setting is monitored for change since any admin can disable it.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Secure: RoleSeparationEnabled = 1, with change monitoring. Insecure: 0 / unset — duties not separated. Enable with certutil -setreg CA\RoleSeparationEnabled 1.
how_to_obtain.source: Microsoft Learn — Securing PKI: Technical Controls for Securing PKI

option_description: Whether ACLs on certificate-template AD objects limit Write/WriteDacl/WriteProperty/FullControl to Domain Admins / dedicated PKI-admin groups, with no such rights for unprivileged principals.
security_impact: An OR-trigger for "Weak / default CA admin access and role separation" — fires when false, where a non-Tier-0 principal holding WriteDacl/WriteProperty/FullControl can reconfigure a benign template into an ESC1 template (ESC4).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Enumerate ACEs on certificate-template AD objects with PSPKIAudit / BloodHound ADCSESC4 edges.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Secure: only Tier-0 admins hold Write rights. Insecure: unprivileged principal with WriteDacl/WriteProperty/FullControl on a template (ESC4).
how_to_obtain.source: SpecterOps — Certified Pre-Owned: Abusing Active Directory Certificate Services (ESC1-ESC8)

option_description: Whether ACLs on PKI infrastructure objects (CA computer object, NTAuthCertificates, CN=Public Key Services PKI containers) are Tier-0-protected with no Write/FullControl for unprivileged principals.
security_impact: An OR-trigger for "Weak / default CA admin access and role separation" — fires when false, where dangerous ACLs on PKI objects/NTAuth enable RBCD or NTAuth poisoning to compromise the CA/forest (ESC5).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Enumerate ACEs over CN=Public Key Services,CN=Services,CN=Configuration with BloodHound ADCSESC5 edges / PSPKIAudit.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Secure: only Tier-0 admins hold Write rights on PKI objects. Insecure: unprivileged principal with WriteDacl/WriteProperty/FullControl on a PKI container/NTAuth (ESC5).
how_to_obtain.source: SpecterOps — Certified Pre-Owned: Abusing Active Directory Certificate Services (ESC1-ESC8)

option_description: Whether the CA publishes a working revocation method — a CRL and/or OCSP responder — with CDP/AIA URLs embedded in issued certificates.
security_impact: An OR-trigger for "Missing or stale revocation lifecycle" — fires when false (no revocation mechanism configured), so a compromised or mis-issued certificate stays trusted until natural expiry with no kill-switch.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect an issued leaf cert for CDP/AIA URLs that point to a revocation method.
how_to_obtain.command: openssl x509 -in leaf.crt -noout -text | grep -A4 -E 'CRL Distribution|Authority Information Access'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Secure: CDP/AIA URLs present pointing to a CRL/OCSP method. Insecure: no CDP/AIA — no revocation configured.
how_to_obtain.source: AWS Private CA — Plan your certificate revocation method

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm a revocation method is selected and managed (OCSP and/or CRL); for cloud/managed CAs verify RevocationConfiguration Crl/Ocsp Enabled = true.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Secure: managed revocation enabled. Insecure: revocation absent — a compromised cert stays trusted until expiry.
how_to_obtain.source: AWS Private CA — Plan your certificate revocation method

option_description: Whether the CDP/AIA URLs embedded in issued certificates are actually reachable by relying parties so CRL/OCSP fetches succeed.
security_impact: An OR-trigger for "Missing or stale revocation lifecycle" — fires when false (dead URL, network-isolated, DNS failure), where relying parties silently fall open and revocation is unenforced even though a method is nominally configured.

how_to_obtain.instruction: From a relying-party vantage point, fetch the CDP/AIA URLs embedded in a leaf cert and confirm they resolve and return current data.
how_to_obtain.command: openssl x509 -in leaf.crt -noout -text | grep -A4 -E 'CRL Distribution|Authority Information Access'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Secure: CDP/AIA URLs present and reachable. Insecure: unreachable URL / DNS failure — revocation fetch fails.
how_to_obtain.source: AWS Private CA — Plan your certificate revocation method

option_description: Whether the published CRL's nextUpdate is in the future (not expired) and OCSP responses carry a short next-update — i.e. revocation data is current.
security_impact: An OR-trigger for "Missing or stale revocation lifecycle" — fires when false (CRL stale/expired), where relying parties may treat it as invalid and fall open, leaving revoked certificates trusted.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Fetch the CRL and check its nextUpdate is in the future; confirm a short configured CRL next-update interval.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Secure: nextUpdate in the future (fresh). Insecure: expired CRL — relying parties may fall open.
how_to_obtain.source: AWS Private CA — Plan your certificate revocation method

option_description: The maximum validity period (in days) the CA grants to leaf certificates. HIGH_IS_INSECURE: an over-long lifetime widens the window a compromised or mis-issued certificate stays usable before natural expiry.
security_impact: An OR-trigger for "Missing or stale revocation lifecycle" — fires when greater than 397 days (the CA/Browser Forum public-TLS leaf ceiling), most damaging precisely when revocation is missing or stale.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read the issuing profile / template validity (EJBCA validity field; AD CS ValidityPeriod/ValidityPeriodUnits).
how_to_obtain.file_path: EJBCA certificate profile / AD CS registry
how_to_obtain.navigation: EJBCA Admin GUI -> Certificate Profiles -> <profile> -> Validity (or certutil -getreg CA\ValidityPeriod / ValidityPeriodUnits)
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Secure: bounded validity (<= 397 days for leaves). Insecure: excessive lifetime widening the trusted window.
how_to_obtain.source: EJBCA (Keyfactor) — Certificate Profile Fields

option_description: Whether the requester CANNOT dictate certificate lifetime (EJBCA 'Allow Validity Override' disabled, or the AD CS template not honouring a requester-supplied notAfter).
security_impact: An OR-trigger for "Missing or stale revocation lifecycle" — fires when false (override enabled), letting an enrollee demand an arbitrary over-long lifetime, widening the trusted window beyond the CA's intended bound.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect the certificate profile's 'Allow Validity Override' setting (must be disabled), or AD CS template notAfter handling.
how_to_obtain.file_path: EJBCA certificate profile / AD CS registry
how_to_obtain.navigation: EJBCA Admin GUI -> Certificate Profiles -> <profile> -> Allow Validity Override
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Secure: Allow Validity Override disabled. Insecure: override enabled — requester dictates lifetime.
how_to_obtain.source: EJBCA (Keyfactor) — Certificate Profile Fields

option_description: The hash algorithm the CA uses in its certificate signatures. SHA-256+ is the modern floor; sha1/md5 are deprecated and produce forgeable signatures.
security_impact: An OR-trigger for "Weak signing algorithm" — fires on in [sha1, md5], undermining the integrity of every certificate the CA signs.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read the issuing CA cert's Signature Algorithm.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Secure: sha256WithRSAEncryption or stronger. Insecure: sha1WithRSAEncryption / md5.
how_to_obtain.source: EJBCA (Keyfactor) — Certificate Profile Fields

how_to_obtain.instruction: EJBCA: check the Certificate Profile signature algorithm; AD CS: read the configured hash algorithm from the registry.
how_to_obtain.file_path: EJBCA certificate profile / AD CS registry
how_to_obtain.navigation: EJBCA Admin GUI -> Certificate Profiles -> <profile> -> Signature Algorithm
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Secure: hash SHA-256+. Insecure: SHA-1 / MD5 permitted.
how_to_obtain.source: EJBCA (Keyfactor) — Certificate Profile Fields

option_description: The CA signing key's algorithm and strength. Floors are RSA >= 2048 (3072+ for long-lived roots) or P-256/P-384 ECDSA; rsa_1024 or smaller is below the floor and brute-forcible.
security_impact: An OR-trigger for "Weak signing algorithm" — fires on in [rsa_1024, rsa_512], a forgeable signing key that undermines the entire chain.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read the issuing CA cert's Public-Key size/algorithm.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Secure: RSA >= 2048 / EC >= 256. Insecure: 1024-bit (or smaller) key.
how_to_obtain.source: EJBCA (Keyfactor) — Certificate Profile Fields

how_to_obtain.instruction: EJBCA: confirm 'Available Bit Lengths' enforces RSA >= 2048 / modern ECC.
how_to_obtain.navigation: EJBCA Admin GUI -> Certificate Profiles -> <profile> -> Available Bit Lengths
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Secure: minimum bit length >= 2048. Insecure: sub-2048 permitted.
how_to_obtain.source: EJBCA (Keyfactor) — Certificate Profile Fields

option_description: Whether the CA records every certificate issuance, revocation, and template change to an audit log across all event categories (AD CS: AuditFilter = 127 AND the OS 'Audit object access' policy enabled Success/Failure).
security_impact: An OR-trigger for "Disabled or non-attributable issuance auditing" — fires when false/partial, where rogue-certificate minting (the goal of every ESC primitive) becomes invisible.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read the CA AuditFilter (127 = all categories) and confirm the OS audit policy 'Audit object access' is enabled, else CA events are not written.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Secure: AuditFilter = 127 and object-access auditing on. Insecure: AuditFilter 0/partial — issuance not logged.
how_to_obtain.source: Microsoft Learn — Securing PKI: Technical Controls for Securing PKI

option_description: Whether CA issuance/revocation/admin audit events are centrally retained by forwarding to a SIEM rather than left only in the local host event log.
security_impact: An OR-trigger for "Disabled or non-attributable issuance auditing" — fires when false, where locally-only logs are non-attributable, clearable on host compromise, and unavailable for PKI-abuse detection across the estate.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm a working forwarder ships CA audit events to a central SIEM / log store off the CA host.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Secure: CA issuance/revocation/admin events appear in the central SIEM. Insecure: events only in the local host event log.
how_to_obtain.source: general-knowledge

option_description: Whether CA administrative actions — template changes, CA security/ACL edits, policy-flag changes (e.g. EDITF_ATTRIBUTESUBJECTALTNAME2), role-separation toggles — are audited and attributable to individual operators.
security_impact: An OR-trigger for "Disabled or non-attributable issuance auditing" — fires when false, where a config-weakening admin action that enables an ESC primitive leaves no attributable trace.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Verify admin/config-change auditing is enabled and that change events are attributable to named operators.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Secure: admin/config-change events logged and attributable to individuals. Insecure: config changes untracked or anonymous.
how_to_obtain.source: general-knowledge

option_description: Whether CA audit logs are tamper-resistant — write-once / off-host retained so a local administrator (or attacker who minted a rogue cert) cannot delete or edit the issuance record.
security_impact: An OR-trigger for "Disabled or non-attributable issuance auditing" — fires when false, where even enabled logs are unreliable evidence because the very subject they would incriminate can clear them.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm logs are write-once / WORM or off-host retained and that local admins cannot edit or clear them.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Secure: WORM / off-host retention; local admins cannot alter logs. Insecure: logs editable/clearable on the CA host.
